ana (runtime): heads-up: after the kernel-selector canary (seq-opt) rolled at 09:12 we've seen a sharp uptick in OOMs on the c4x cluster for requests > 1024 tokens. error spike started ~09:20 UTC.

mike (infra): copying the OOM logs now. any repro steps?

ana (runtime): (typo) ana :) repro is intermittent but easy to trigger with a mixed batch: one 2048-token request + several 64-token requests. profiler shows workspace allocations ballooning per-request when seq-opt chooses the long-kernel path.

cheng: logs?

ana (runtime): pasted sample snippet from one of the failing workers:

```
[2021-09-21T09:21:44Z] allocate_workspace(model=xl-1, seq_len=2048) -> requested=1450 MiB, reserved_pool=1024 MiB, fallback_alloc=426 MiB
[2021-09-21T09:21:44Z] OOM: unable to reserve workspace. batch_tokens=4096, kernel=kv-opt-long, allocator_state: free=64MiB, frag=87%
```

rachel (mlperf): profiler counters for that time window show per-request median memory +120MiB and tail +420MiB vs baseline. Also observed kernel switch increased temporary buffer allocations for attention tiling.

mike (infra): this looks like a fragmentation/regression combo. Did seq-opt change kernel tiling or add an extra temp buffer?

ana (runtime): seq-opt tightened tiling to reduce kernel launches for long sequences; it now allocs an extra workspace slice for fused softmax for long-kernel path. Good perf normally but when we mix batch lengths it duplicates buffers per sample in the batcher.

cheng: actionable ideas: 1) make kernel selector sequence-length aware at batch level (choose per-batch kernel by max_seq instead of per-sample), 2) add protective cap to workspace allocation per-device, 3) tweak batcher to avoid co-mingling very long samples with short ones.

rachel (mlperf): I ran a quick sim: using per-batch kernel (max_seq heuristic) reduced peak memory by ~30% on mixed loads. Batching policy change had minimal latency impact for long requests but improved tail OOMs.

mike (infra): deploy-bot how many canaries were hit?

deploy-bot: canary roll: 12 hosts total. 5 hosts reported OOMs after canary. Automatic canary pause initiated at 09:29 UTC.

ana (runtime): proposing interim mitigations while we patch seq-opt: - set workspace_budget_mb per model to 512 for canary models, - enforce batch_mixing_threshold_tokens=256 (do not mix samples with token diff > threshold), - decrease kernel-selector aggressive mode to "safe" for canary.

cheng: +1. Also propose adding allocator-level slab coalescing patch to reduce fragmentation (cheap path). I can sketch quick allocator tweak: coalesce_free_adjacent() and prefer reusing recently-freed slabs for workspace pools.

rachel (mlperf): also let's not forget prefix cache pressure. When workspace fails we fall back to loading more KV blocks which increases mem churn. For prompt cache: increasing shard_count reduces per-shard working set but raises overhead; we should experiment with shard_count=48 -> 80 and TTL drop from 3600s->900s for short-lived workloads. hit-rate model predicts 6% hit-drop but 22% lower resident memory.

mike (infra): can you post the config patch you'll try?

ana (runtime): posting canary patch suggestion:

```
# runtime canary overrides
kernel_selector.mode = "safe"  # disable seq-opt aggressive tiling
workspace_budget_mb = 512
batching.batch_mixing_threshold_tokens = 256
kv_prefixcache.shard_count = 64
kv_prefixcache.shard_ttl_s = 900
allocator.coalesce_adjacent = true
```

cheng: rx. I'll bundle allocator coalesce as a feature-flagged change. We'll run perf smoke and fragmentation check: measure free-slab-count and frag% before/after.

rachel (mlperf): I'll run the hit-rate sim across three workload mixes (chatty, long-form, mixed) and post results in #eng-runtime. Early read: mixed workloads benefit most from batch-mixing threshold change.

mike (infra): action items: 1) revert seq-opt in canary (deploy bot did pause) or set to safe — ana will push patch, 2) cheng to push allocator coalesce flag and run unit smoke, 3) rachel to validate prefixcache shard/TTL tradeoffs, 4) we'll run a 2-hour soak on 6 hosts.

ana (runtime): pushing patch now to canary via CLI:
```
redwoodctl deploy canary --hosts=6 --overrides ./canary_runtime_patch.yaml
```

deploy-bot: started canary update on hosts [h3,h7,h12,h18,h19,h21] at 09:42 UTC. Monitor: /dash/infra/canary/2021502468

mike (infra): thanks. if we still see OOMs after these mitigations we'll probably need to revert kernel-selector permanently until we have per-batch heuristics.

cheng: will instrument allocator with extra counters: slab_reuse_rate, avg_free_chunk_size. coming in next 30m.

rachel (mlperf): ping me once coalesce flag is up; I'll re-run sim with updated allocator numbers.

ana (runtime): thanks everyone. I'll keep posting logs and the canary dashboard link. :thumbsup:
